threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look baffled when the bus driver yells at you for not having your Oyster card ready. We know that confusion well.
Saw a guy on the night bus last week, he was drumming on his backpack like it was a bongo. Didn't miss a beat even when we hit that pothole!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a kid selling homemade lemonade on the corner, while their mom haggled over a bike in broken German. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, the kebab shops are open at all hours, but it’s the breakfast döner at 6 AM that hits different—crispy and surprisingly fresh.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know you’re local when you can spot the tourists taking selfies with the murals but can’t remember the last time you did.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a guy playing sax on the 19 bus, but no one noticed. Meanwhile, two pigeons were having a full-blown fight on the steps of the Civic Center station.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the quiet streets of Gràcia are always bustling. But at 3 PM on a Wednesday, it's like a ghost town, just the locals sipping café.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment at how many times a single bus can be late. Locals either expect it or just walk.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still wait for a bus like it’s on time, instead of checking your phone for the next arrival—and it’s always late.
Heard a guy on the 196 bragging about finding a bag of cash in a park. Sketchy vibes but the way he told it, you’d think it was a film plot.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw the guy at the corner café crafting an espresso while discussing the latest BVG strike with a complete stranger. That’s Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you ride a tram while sharing a seat with someone’s pet iguana. It’s weirdly charming and part of the city’s quirky vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they can name all the taco trucks on 24th St without blinking, but a visitor still thinks ‘taco truck’ means a food court.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the N-Judah today; a guy serenading commuters with a ukulele. Only in the Tenderloin would you find a pop-up concert at 8 AM.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just the park and pretty squares, but the real vibe is in the tiny, tucked-away bars where locals sip vermut and chat for hours.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their hesitation at the pedestrian crossings; they still wait for the light even when locals just dash across.
